verdict.rationale: LM Studio's own docs say it serves local models on OpenAI-like endpoints "locally and on the network," and the 0.3.0 release notes describe a toggle that opens the server to requests from outside localhost. The server can also be started from the CLI and runs headless via llmster. One community user could not work out how to use it over the LAN, but that is a discoverability complaint, not a concrete failure. Missing for 10: detailed docs on network binding, port and authentication, and independent hands-on confirmation of access from another device.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can serve models over my local network for access from other devices

citations.quote: Serve local models on OpenAI-like endpoints, locally and on the network
Turning this on will open up the server to requests outside of 'localhost'.
Start and stop the local server ... lms server start / lms server stop
llmster is the headless version of LM Studio, no desktop app required. It's ideal for servers, CI environments, or any machine where you don't need a GUI.
